main_body: Red barn: a large tiled roof slope (rows 1-57) over a vertical plank front wall with a double door and two windows (rows 58-90) on a stone base
top_band: Roof slope, x=47: cream eave highlight at rows 1-3, then scalloped red-orange tiles at rows 9-55 (L 72-110), closed by a cream front-edge line at rows 56-57
evidence: The tiled roof reads as a large foreshortened top slope, as on the reference houses. A cream edge line at rows 56-57 ends it, and a dark eave row sits right below it at about row 58. Under that is the front wall with a vertical plank face, a stone base, and a dark-framed door and windows that look inset. The dormer on the roof also shows its own slope. The roof and the front wall are both drawn correctly, so the contract holds.

style.evidence: The roof has scalloped tiles in about five steps: cream, orange, light red, mid red and deep maroon. The wall has vertical plank stripes and the stone base is dithered. The outline is a dark brown and has 0% neutral pixels, so it is tinted and not a black sticker line. There are no flat 5x5 fills (0%). The candidate has 7 colours per tile against 11 and 18 for the references, and only 23 distinct colours against 66 and 185. The doors and window frames are plain light grey and the wall has only about three tones, so it is thinner than the references. It is still acceptable next to them.
